version.value: Romance for violin and orchestra; the orchestral version made in 1920, first played in June 1921.
version.note: The Internet Archive description and the Discogs label credit call it a Romance for violin and orchestra. The performing edition is not identified, and nothing in the item points to cuts across its four sides.

performers.note: Both sources name the three. The Archive description adds a presumption that Wise was the orchestra’s leader; that is not independently established here.

catalogue.note: The Archive item gives September 1947 as the issue month. Discogs dates the UK set to 1947 and notes the “ST” tax code (April 1946 – November 1947).

matrixTakeSides.value: Matrices CAX 9863 to 9866, all first takes (four sides)
matrixTakeSides.note: Stated in the Archive item’s description. The labels and stampers were not examined for this dossier.

credits.note: The item is filed in that collection; no transfer engineer is named in the description.

date.note: The Archive upload date (2 April 2022) is not a transfer date.

processing.value: FLAC original with a variable-bitrate MP3 derivative, joined from four 78-rpm sides into one file.
processing.note: Equalisation, speed correction and noise reduction are not documented.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of a 78-rpm transfer

composition.value: Vaughan Williams’s copyright in the music runs to the end of 2028 in the UK and EU.
composition.note: The Vaughan Williams Foundation gives 2028 as the year copyright in his music expires. Composition rights are separate from the recording.

recording.value: Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: commercial issue in 1947, before 1963
recording.note: The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies to this 1947 Columbia set: its former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is not United States or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

rights.creditLine: Ralph Vaughan Williams, The Lark Ascending; David Wise, Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra, Malcolm Sargent. English Columbia DX 1386–1387 (1947), Internet Archive transfer.
